text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE NEWS
- The Central Development Working party of the Planning Commission has approved the second Karachi port modernisation project-VI costing 12.92 billion rupees.

- Morgan Grenfell, the advisory company for the privatisation of 26 percent of the shares in the Pakistan Telecommunication Corporation, has informed the Privatisation Commission that the chances of foreign investment appear to be remote because of political instability in Pakistan.
- The government is considering increasing the price of natural gas by November 30.
DAWN
- Chief Justice Sajjad Ali Shah said the Supreme Court would interpret the articles of the Constitution in a manner that would not destroy the federal character of the country.
- President Farooq Leghari presided over a high level meeting on the security situation in the region with special reference to Kashmir and Afghanistan.
- The accountability process kicked off after the Chief Ehtesab (accountability) Commissioner Ghulam Mujaddid Mirza formally took charge of his office on Tuesday.

- Wajid Shamsul Hasan, former high commissioner of Pakistan to Britian, was arrested and booked by the Federal Investigation Agency and accused of misappropriating government funds to the tune of 200,000 pounds sterling.

- Caretaker foreign minister Sahabzada Yaqub Khan is due to leave for Washington in early December for the first high-level contact with the U.S. administration on behalf of the caretaker government following the re-election of President Bill Clinton
- A strong group of dissidents from former prime minister Benazir Bhutto's party is planning to take over the party and expel Bhutto and her associates at a party convention on December 1.
- Federal Law Minister Fakhruddin Ebrahim said five more ordinances would be issued by President Farooq Leghari to ensure the accountability process was transparent and useful.
- Former chairman of state-run Pakistan Steel Mills Sajjad Hussain was detained by federal investigators, sources said.
- U.S. Consul General in Karachi Douglas Archard said the reason for low U.S. investment in Pakistan compared to other countries in Asia was Pakistan's economic policies and not political turmoil.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The World Bank has asked the government to slash budgetary allocation for the 300 megawatt Chashma Nuclear Power Plant.
- The government is planing to install a $45 million single point mooring facility for oil tankers at Khalifa Point near Karachi to feed the proposed Pak-Iran oil refinery.
FINANCIAL POST
- The state-run National Bank of Pakistan has withdrawn the condition of charging any banking margin before sanctioning loans for gold imports, sources said.
- HG Asia (Holdings) Ltd, has doubled its stake in First Capital Securities, a local brokerage house, to 40 percent from 20 percent.
- The caretaker government has launched an austerity plan for state-owned banks and financial instituions.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
